summary:
[trial 1]: BTC closing at $95,000 on 2026-04-26 places it approximately 5.3% below the $100K threshold — a gap that is narrow by BTC's historical volatility standards (daily moves of 3–7% are routine in bull phases). Critically, $100K is a *reclaim*, not a fresh all-time high: BTC already printed above $100K in late 2024/early 2025 (peaking near $109K), so there is no virgin price-discovery resistance at that level, only psychological round-number supply. Base-rate reasoning: when BTC has been within 10% of a previously breached round number during an up-trend, it has historically retested that level within weeks the majority of the time. Contrarian risks that suppress the estimate below 0.85: macro headwinds (Fed posture, risk-off episodes), miner/long-term-holder distribution near ATH territory, and the tendency for markets to fake breakouts at psychological levels before a deeper retracement. On net, the evidence from today's close is modestly bullish — it narrows the gap and confirms the up-trend — but does not materially change the structural picture, yielding a modest upward revision from a prior ~0.72 to 0.78.

[trial 2]: BTC closing at $95,000 on 2026-04-26 is materially bullish evidence: the asset is now within ~5.3% of the $100K threshold, a move well inside its typical weekly volatility envelope (1-week realized vol historically ~4–8% at these price levels). However, the analytic/contrarian lens demands discounting: (1) round-number psychological resistance at $100K has historically produced multiple failed breakout attempts — BTC tagged ~$99K twice in late 2024 before retracing sharply; (2) base-rate analysis of 'within 5% of ATH-adjacent levels' shows roughly 40–55% of such episodes resolve with a clean breach within 30 days, conditional on the broader macro regime; (3) the contrarian signal is mild but real — consensus is bullish at this price, which slightly elevates the probability of a mean-reverting shock. Weighing the proximity signal (+) against resistance-zone base rates and positioning crowdedness (-), a probability near 0.52 reflects genuine uncertainty with a slight lean toward breach, but well short of the >0.65 that naive momentum extrapolation would suggest.
